LESSON: PHYSICAL ASPECT OF YOGA

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Yoga (Holistic Wellness)
Topic 6.1: Physical Aspect of Yoga
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Physical Aspect of Yoga, part of Yoga (Holistic Wellness) in Grade 5 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why are Asanas important in performin g Yoga? 2. How does Pranayam help in physical wellbeing ?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. using digital devices, like YouTube and demonstrative manuals and correctly perform Pranayam and Asanas,

2. visit and participate in the celebration of International Yoga Day,

3. practise Asanas with peers.

4. create a Yoga guidance video using digital devices,

5. sing/recite song/poem on Yoga that they are familiar with,

6. discuss types of Pranayam with the guidance of the teacher,

7. Assist peers with special needs in practicing Pranayams as per their ability to perform. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. using digital devices, like YouTube and demonstrative manuals and correctly perform Pranayam and Asanas,
2. visit and participate in the celebration of International Yoga Day,
3. practise Asanas with peers.
4. create a Yoga guidance video using digital devices,
5. sing/recite song/poem on Yoga that they are familiar with,
6. discuss types of Pranayam with the guidance of the teacher,
7. Assist peers with special needs in practicing Pranayams as per their ability to perform. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Physical Aspect of Yoga together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: Learner enhances working collaboratively when practising Asanas, in pairs and groups, to encourage and

help each other.

Values:
Patriotism: Learner observes citizenship when visiting and participating in the celebration of International Yoga Day.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Learner exhibits nationality when visiting and participating in the celebration of International Yoga Day.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learner is able to relate the skill of using digital devices to look for appropriate videos from YouTube and demonstrative

manuals and correctly perform the Pranayams to the skills of using digital devices learnt in Creative Arts.

CSL AT UPPER PRIMARY (GRADE 4 – 6)

At this level, the goal of the CSL activity is to provide linkages between the concepts learnt in various learning activities and

the real-life experiences. Learners begin to make connections between what they learn and the relevance to their daily

life. CSL is hosted in the Social Studies learning area. The implementation is a collaborative effort where the class

teacher coordinates and works with other subject teachers to design and implement the integrated CSL activity. Though

they are teacher-guided, the learners should progressively be given more autonomy to identify problems and come up

with solutions. The safety of the learners should also be taken into account when selecting the CSL activity. The following

steps for the integrated CSL activity should be staggered across the school terms:

Steps in carrying out the integrated CSL activity

1. Preparation

• Map out the targeted core competencies, values and specific learning areas skills for the CSL activity

• Identify resources required for the activity (locally available material
s) • Stagger the activities across the term (set dates and time for the activitie
s) • Communicate to learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teachers and other relevant

stakeholders in the school community

• Identify and develop assessment tools

2. Implementation of the CSL Activity

• Assign roles to learners.

• Ensure every learner actively participates in the activity

• Observe learners as they carry out the CSL activity and record feedback

• Use an appropriate assessment tool to assess both the process and the product (asess learner’s work from the

beginning to the end produc
t) • Assess the targeted core competencies, values and subject skills.

33

3. Reflection on the CSL Activity

Conduct a self-evaluation session with learners on the integrated CSL activity undertaken by discussing the

following:

• what went well and why

• what did not go well and why

• what can be done differently next time

• what they have learnt.
